title: Dot and Olive's Sunny Hill Adventure
markdown:
Once, right by a sparkly splashy pond, lived Dot the duckling and Olive the owl. The pond had lily pads that bobbed like little green hats, and tall reeds that whispered secrets in the breezy air. Dot was a little ball of sunshine-yellow fluff, so soft you’d want to give her a big squeeze. Her feet did a funny happy waddle, always eager to go somewhere new. Every day she would waddle everywhere she could dream up, sometimes just circles around her favourite dandelion patch, pitter-patter along the ground. Olive was a super-duper wise owl. Her big round eyes twinkled like little moons, and her feathers were fluffier than a cloud. She loved sitting in her cozy tree nook, reading books packed with zingy facts and funny poems. She knew amazing things, like how a butterfly tastes with its feet.

Every day Dot practised her most splendid waddle. Pitter-patter and wobble-wobble, and sometimes a happy little hop just because. She’d pretend she was off to discover a brand-new land, even if it was just to the big oak tree at the edge of the pond. Olive would hoot out amazing facts. “Did you know a snail has a nose on its head?” “A group of owls is called a parliament.” Olive thought that was a very funny idea. But as much as they loved their pond, they both secretly wished for something a little more exciting. They often looked out toward Sunny Hill, the tippy-top of the biggest tallest hill around, and peeked through the tall grass at the very top of the lighthouse, like a friendly finger pointing up to the sky.

Until one day, whoosh. A most funny thing happened. A wiggly jiggly parcel, tied with a string that looked like it was doing a little dance, landed right at Dot’s webbed feet with a gentle thump. Brown paper that smelled like far-off adventures. Bright red ribbons that seemed to wink. In neat fancy letters: To the Lighthouse Keeper, Sunny Hill.

“A parcel,” quacked Dot, and her waddle went into super-duper overdrive.

“For the lighthouse,” hooted Olive, big eyes wide.

Because of that, they decided they would take it there. A parcel this important needed a very special delivery. They carefully picked it up. It felt a little bit ticklish. It wiggled and jiggled as if it had a tiny happy creature hiding inside.

First they had to cross the giggling brook. Not a big brook, but a wobbly bridge of smooth grey stones that sparkled in the sun. Dot went first, her waddle turning into a careful tip-toe-waddle, eyes looking straight ahead. “Wheee. This is like a dance, Olive.” The water below made little splish-splash sounds, like it was laughing with her. Olive flew just above, soft wings making a gentle whoosh. “Careful, little waddler.”

Because of that, they started climbing the grassy path up Sunny Hill. A long happy climb, full of fluffy dandelions and cheerful daisies that seemed to smile. Bumblebees buzzed past, fuzzy little bodies dusted with yellow pollen. The sun made everything smell warm and sweet, like honey and freshly cut grass. Dot’s waddle kept going, a steady determined rhythm. Olive flapped her wings gently, keeping Dot company. “Look, Dot. A ladybug with seven spots.” They saw bright red ladybugs and fluffy white clouds that looked like giant sheep having a nap in the sky. The parcel wiggled a little less now, as if it was getting excited to arrive too.

Until finally they reached the very top. The lighthouse was tall and bright, painted a cheerful white with red stripes, and a shiny round window at the very top that twinkled in the sun. It looked like a friendly giant watching over everything. Tap, tap, tap went Dot’s little beak on the big sturdy red door. She waddled back and forth, her whole body a-wiggle. Creeeak. The door opened. A surprise was waiting, not a scary one. It smelled delicious, like warm cookies, and a happy rumbling sound came from inside.

Out popped a cheerful man with a bushy white beard that looked like a fluffy cloud and a bright blue hat that looked like it had seen a million sunsets. The lighthouse keeper. A kind smile that crinkled the corners of his eyes. He had been expecting the parcel. He was holding a big colourful bouquet of flowers.

“Ah, my delivery,” he boomed, his voice warm like a cozy blanket. He took the wiggly parcel, which gave a final little wiggle as if to say goodbye. He gave Dot a gentle tickle under her chin, which made her do a happy little quack-wiggle, and Olive a friendly nod. “Thank you, my friends. You have brought me something very special.” He carefully opened the parcel, and inside was a beautiful shiny red apple. It smelled so sweet. “And for your excellent delivery, I have a treat for you too.” He pulled out a big plate piled high with warm crumbly biscuits that smelled like sunshine and cinnamon.

Dot and Olive munched happily. The biscuits were so tasty they made their little tummies do a happy dance. They sat there, side by side, the lighthouse keeper humming a happy tune.

Ever since then Dot’s waddle was even happier on the path home, and Olive’s nook held a new tale, and Sunny Hill did not feel quite so far.
